When multiple planets are in Virgo in your natal chart, this can give you strong Virgo energy in your life and personality. You can be practical, detailed, and focused. This can be the case if you have a Virgo stellium (3+ planets in one Zodiac sign), or if you have 2 of your primary triad (Sun, Moon, Rising) in Virgo.

You can also feel that you have strong Virgo energy if your natal Mercury is strong, which is the planet that rules Virgo (especially in an earth or water sign). This can be the case if your natal Mercury is conjunct your natal Sun, Moon or Ascendant, or your 1st house ruler, or if your natal Mercury is a singleton (only planet in an element, modality, or house type).

When multiple transit planets are in Virgo, this gives all of us a strong dose of Virgo energy all at once. We're all hard-working and practical. How we end up feeling this personally is usually focused on the house in your natal chart the Virgo energy occurs in.
explain.sign.virgo.strong.subject: Virgo

explain.intro.astrology-charts.overview.title: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.overview.text: When you're getting started with serious astrology, one of the very basics you need to learn about is the various astrology charts. You use charts in a variety of ways with your interpretations and analysis.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.overview.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.overview.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is a natal chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text:
A natal chart (or colloquially, a birth chart) is a snapshot of the exact location in the Zodiac everything was at the moment you were born from the location you were born at.

A standard natal chart has the 10 planets, which includes the Sun and Moon as planets (dubbed the luminaries), but excludes the Earth (so it's Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto). Each planet rules something different in your life and personality, and has its own energy.

A standard natal chart also has the 12 houses. The 12 houses also rule different parts of your life and personality, and have their own energy. Each house correlates to a sign and planet. They are:

1st house: Mars and Aries

2nd house: Venus and Taurus

3rd house: Mercury and Gemini

4th house: Moon and Cancer

5th house: Sun and Leo

6th house: Mercury and Virgo

7th house: Venus and Libra

8th house: Pluto and Scorpio

9th house: Jupiter and Sagittarius

10th house: Saturn and Capricorn

11th house: Uranus and Aquarius

12th house: Neptune and Pisces

There are different ways of calculating the houses, and these are called house systems. There's a bunch of them, but the most commonly used (at least in the West) would be Placidus, Koch, Equal, and Whole Sign.

There are also the angles, which are the Ascendant, Imum Coeli, Descendant, and Midheaven. In Placidus (and Koch), the Ascendant in the 1st house cusp, the Imum Coeli is the 4th house cusp, the Descendant is the 7th house cusp, and the Midheaven is the 10th house cusp. The cusp of a house is the very beginning of that house.

With Equal, the Ascendant is the 1st house cusp, and each subsequent house follows in the same degree and minute of the signs in order (unless it's using the Midheaven instead of the Ascendant, and then it'll have the Midheaven as the 10th house cusp, and each subsequent house following in the same degree and minute in order). With Whole Sign, the Ascendant sign is the sign of the 1st house, and each house goes in order, and all are at 0 degrees.

Every sign in astrology is made up of 30 degrees; each degree is made up of 60 minutes; and each minute is made up of 60 seconds (just like time!). This helps to pinpoint the exact location of planets and other points in a chart.

Some charts will also have other points, like asteroids.

The natal chart shows who you are. Everything in your natal chart is a map for your personality and life. That's probably the most helpful way of looking at your natal chart - it's the map of you!

This map is outlined by focusing on your natal planets (the what), their sign location (the how), and their house location (the where). Signs on the house cusps show how the energy of that house is expressed in your life. Your natal planets at certain angles to one another can create positive connections between them, or challenges. There's a lot to unpack in a natal chart!

You can also use the natal chart in predictive analysis by tracking the transit (moving) planets (and other bodies) and how they interact with your natal chart. They can move through your natal houses and come to certain angles to your natal planets and have an impact on your life.

A natal chart requires 3 pieces of data:

date of birth

time of birth

place of birth

Date and time of birth determine the exact location of the planets; place of birth comes into play for the houses.

Also note that sometimes natal charts are referred to as birth charts (however natal chart is the correct technical term).
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is a progressed chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text: With a progressed chart, one day is added to your date of birth for every year you've been alive (how old you are) to create a new chart, the progressed chart. This chart is reflective of how you change and grow with age. The natal chart remains a fixed constant, but we do change over time. The progressed chart is where that's shown. The progressed chart is also used in predictive analysis. It can be used by itself, when your progressed planets and house cusps change signs or come to certain angles to one another. It can also be compared against your natal chart, and you can track the transit planets and how they interact with your progressed chart as well.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is a return chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text:
A return occurs when one of the transit planets returns to the exact location it was at when you were born. A return chart is a chart created for that moment when it happens. Return charts can show how that specific return may impact you. This is a part of predictive analysis.

The most commonly used return chart is the solar return chart, which is the return of the transit Sun to your natal Sun location, and this happens once each year around your birthday.

To create a return chart, you need the date and time of the return, and the location you were at when it occurred.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is an event chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text:
An event chart creates a "natal chart" for an event. This may be used to analyze events that have already occurred to see what astrological energy was present and contributed to it, and it can be used to analyze future events you know will happen so you can see the energy around it.

To create an event chart, you need the date, time, and location of the event.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is an horary chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text: An horary chart is used to answer specific questions. The chart is created for the moment the question is asked (location can vary, it may be your location if you're doing it yourself, or the location of the astrologer interpreting it for you if you're having someone else do it). The chart is then analyzed to find an answer to the question.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is a relocation chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text: A relocation chart is your natal chart, but the place of birth is swapped out and replaced by your current place of residence. Birth time may need to be adjusted if it's in a different time zone (add or subtract whatever the difference is). You're always your natal chart personality-wise (and absorb your progressed chart), but the relocation chart can be used for predictive analysis, tracking transit planet interactions to it.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.lineage: relocation · the natal chart at another horizon
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.title: What is a composite chart?
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.text: A composite chart merges the charts of two people and creates a new chart for the relationship itself. It can be analyzed for compatibility, and compared to each person's chart. Transits can also be tracked to it, and it can be progressed. Composite charts are a part of relationship astrology.
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.subject: Intro to Astrology Charts
explain.intro.astrology-charts.q.what-is.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Charts

explain.intro.astrology-houses.overview.title: Intro to Astrology Houses
explain.intro.astrology-houses.overview.text: Astrology has lots of different points to decipher, from planets to asteroids, fixed stars to midpoints, various charts, and more, and one of the most important to understand are the astrology houses.
explain.intro.astrology-houses.overview.subject: Intro to Astrology Houses
explain.intro.astrology-houses.overview.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Houses

explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-ar.title: What are the astrology houses?
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-ar.text:
There are 12 houses in astrology, and each rule a different part of your life and personality. There are a variety of ways of calculating their exact positions in the Zodiac, and these are called house systems. The most commonly used in the West are Placidus, Koch, Equal, and Whole Sign.

The houses are also divided up by house type: angular, succedent, and cadent. The angular houses are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, and are connected to the cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn). Their keyword is action. The succedent houses are the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, and are connected to the fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius). Their keyword is fixed. The cadent houses are the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th house, and are connected to the mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces). Their keyword is adaptable.

You'll first and foremost focus on the sign the house cusp falls in (the cusp of a house is the very beginning of that house). You'll then see if there are any planets in the house. Houses that have multiple planets tend to get more attention from you and play a bigger role in your life, while empty houses usually mean there isn't much for you to work out with it in this life (less baggage). You can also take a look at the natural ruler of the sign on the house cusp in your natal chart and get some further insights (the sign and house location of the ruler in your natal chart can tie into the house).
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-ar.subject: Intro to Astrology Houses
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-ar.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Houses

explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-do.title: What do the houses mean in astrology?
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-do.text: Each house has rulership over different parts of you and your life. Let's do a rundown of each astrology house:
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-do.subject: Intro to Astrology Houses
explain.intro.astrology-houses.q.what-do.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Astrology Houses

explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.overv.title: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.overv.text: Astrology focuses on a variety of points to interpret to glean information from, about your personality, your life, your past, and your future. One of the most important points? The planets! So when you're getting started with astrology, you need to understand the planets in astrology.
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.overv.subject: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.overv.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.title: What are the planets in astrology?
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.text:
There are 10 planets in astrology. They include the Sun and Moon (called the luminaries), and exclude the Earth. In order, they are the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto.

Each planet rules a different part of our personalities and lives. Each planet rules different signs and houses. Each planet has its own energy.

Note: I personally also use Ceres, which is technically a dwarf planet (like Pluto).
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.subject: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.title: What signs and houses do the planets rule?
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.text:
Let's break down which signs and houses each planet rules:

The Sun rules Leo and the 5th house

The Moon rules Cancer and the 4th house

Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo and the 3rd and 6th houses

Venus rules Taurus and Libra and the 2nd and 7th houses

Mars rules Aries and the 1st house

Jupiter rules Sagittarius and the 9th house

Saturn rules Capricorn and the 10th house

Uranus rules Aquarius and the 11th house

Neptune rules Pisces and the 12th house

Pluto rules Scorpio and the 8th house

These are the modern rulerships; modern rulerships use Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto. When we didn't have those three planets (before they were known), Saturn ruled Aquarius and the 11th house instead of Uranus, Jupiter ruled Pisces and the 512th house instead of Neptune, and Mars ruled Scorpio and the 8th house instead of Pluto.

Some current astrologers still use those old rulerships, depending on what kind of astrology they practice. There's really not a right or wrong, and you can experiment when you get further in your studies.

Ceres is argued to be the ruler of Taurus instead of Venus; I tend to use Ceres for prediction and consider both Ceres and Venus in the natal chart for Taurus.
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.subject: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.whi.title: Which part of your life and personality does each planet in astrology rule?
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.whi.text:
The Sun: rules the self, who you are to those who know you best, the true you; also rules your physical body

The Moon: rules your emotional self, what you need for emotional stability and security and how you express yourself emotionally; also rules your home/family and internal foundation/core

Mercury: rules the mind, how you communicate and express yourself and connect with your immediate environment; also rules your everyday life

Venus: rules money and relationships, what you value, your approach to relationships and commitment; also rules the other people in your life and the feminine

Mars: rules energy and drive, what drives you to take action and how you take that action when you do; also rules the masculine

Jupiter: rules expansion, how and where you can expand in your life and use opportunity; also rules your beliefs and higher learning

Saturn: rules limitation, the lessons you have to learn and where you can struggle in life until you learn them; also rules your goals and responsibilities

Uranus: rules change, how and where you experience or create changes in your life; also rules independence and your hopes/dreams for the future

Neptune: rules spiritual self, how and where you connect spiritually; also rules how and where you may struggle to be realistic

Pluto: rules transformations, how and where you experience and create deep transformations in your life; also rules shared resources and what you hold deep inside

Ceres: rules nourishment, support, resources, and finances

This is mostly focused on natal astrology.
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.whi.subject: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.whi.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.title: What is the energy of each planet in astrology?
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.text:
The Sun: shines a light, brings attention to whatever it's touching

The Moon: brings emotional energy and emotional focus

Mercury: brings mental focus, ideas, and increases activity

Venus: brings pleasant energy and ease

Mars: brings energy and drive, makes things happen

Jupiter: brings expansive energy, opportunity, and positivity

Saturn: brings restrictive energy, stability when positive

Uranus: brings change energy, sometimes erratic

Neptune: brings foggy energy, intuition and imagination

Pluto: brings transforming energy, can be destructive and powerful

Ceres: brings nourishing energy and focus on resources

This is focused on predictive astrology. As the moving planets make contact to your natal chart, this is the energy each planet brings to you.
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.subject: Intro to Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.planets-in-astrology.q.wha.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.title: Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.text:
When you're getting into learning astrology, one thing that you'll stumble upon is ruling planets. There are ten planets, including the Sun and Moon and excluding the Earth, and each planet ruling a different sign. They go like this:

The Sun rules Leo

The Moon rules Cancer

Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo

Venus rules Taurus and Libra

Mars rules Aries

Jupiter rules Sagittarius

Saturn rules Capricorn

Uranus rules Aquarius

Neptune rules Pisces

Pluto rules Scorpio

I should note, these are the modern rulerships, which include Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto/; before they came around, Jupiter ruled Sagittarius and Pisces, Saturn ruled Capricorn and Aquarius, and Mars ruled Aries and Scorpio. These are called the traditional rulers now.
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.subject: Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.overview.title: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.overview.text: One of the single most basic parts of astrology is the thing that probably everyone starts with - the Zodiac signs! Many are familiar with Zodiac signs when it comes to their horoscopes. This correlates to your Sun sign, the Zodiac sign the Sun was in when you were born. But there are the ten planets who are in their own signs, the 12 houses who are in their own signs, thousands of asteroids in their own signs, and more!
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.overview.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.overview.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.what-are-th.title: What are the Zodiac signs in astrology?
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.what-are-th.text:
There are 12 Zodiac signs in astrology. In order, they are:

Aries

Taurus

Gemini

Cancer

Leo

Virgo

Libra

Scorpio

Sagittarius

Capricorn

Aquarius

Pisces

Each Zodiac sign builds on the previous sign, so each sign comes with the lessons learned of the signs before it. The final sign, Pisces, is seen as knowing all experience as a result, while the first sign, Aries, is seen as the newborn of the Zodiac.

Each sign has an opposite sign with similar yet opposite energy. The opposing signs are:

Aries opposes Libra

Taurus opposes Scorpio

Gemini opposes Sagittarius

Cancer opposes Capricorn

Leo opposes Aquarius

Virgo opposes Pisces
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.what-are-th.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.what-are-th.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.how-are-the.title: How are the Zodiac signs split up?
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.how-are-the.text:
There are two ways that the Zodiac signs are split up: by element and by quality (or modality). By element, they are:

Fire: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius

Earth: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn

Air: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius

Water: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces

By quality, they are:

Cardinal: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn

Fixed: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius

Mutable: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.how-are-the.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.q.how-are-the.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-elements-.title: The Elements & the Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-elements-.text:
Zodiac signs of the same element have a natural base energy that's the same. They're highly compatible, so this is a big part of relationship astrology to gauge compatibility.

The fire signs are highly energized, enthusiastic, and creative. The earth signs are highly practical, productive, and stable. The air signs are highly sociable, intellectual, and diplomatic. The water signs are highly emotional, intuitive, and nurturing.
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-elements-.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-elements-.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-qualities.title: The Qualities & the Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-qualities.text:
Zodiac signs of the same quality also have some base energy that's the same, but there's usually more friction involved. Signs of the same element have a natural ease and harmony between them. Signs of the same quality can have more heat, but also butt heads.

Cardinal signs are the ones who take action. Fixed signs are the ones who keep things going. Mutable signs are the ones who adapt.
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-qualities.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.the-qualities.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.zodiac-signs-.title: Zodiac Signs & the Planets & Houses
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.zodiac-signs-.text:
Each Zodiac sign has a natural ruling planet, and a house that it naturally connects to. They are:

Aries: ruled by Mars, connects to the 1st house of the self

Taurus: ruled by Venus, connects to the 2nd house of money

Gemini: ruled by Mercury, connects to the 3rd house of the mind

Cancer: ruled by the Moon, connects to the 4th house of home/family and emotion Leo: ruled by the Sun, connects to the 5th house of love and creativity Virgo: ruled by Mercury, connects to the 6th house of work, health, and daily life Libra: ruled by Venus, connects to the 7th house of relationships

Scorpio: ruled by Pluto, connects to the 8th house of transformations and shared resources

Sagittarius: ruled by Jupiter, connects to the 9th house of expansion and higher learning

Capricorn: ruled by Saturn, connects to the 10th house of goals and direction Aquarius: ruled by Uranus, connects to the 11th house of friends and dreams Pisces: ruled by Neptune, connects to the 12th house of spirituality and endings
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.zodiac-signs-.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.zodiac-signs-.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.zodiac-signs.how-the-zodia.title: How the Zodiac Signs Build on One Another
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.how-the-zodia.text:
Aries is the first sign, and is the astrological newborn. This makes Aries the sign that wants to take initiative and get things started. Aries has lots of energy as a fire and cardinal sign. It can be impulsive and impatient, but also pioneering. Taurus is the second sign, and has learned patience that Aries lacked. Whatever Taurus starts, it wants to finish once it does. Taurus takes its time, not feeling the rush. Taurus is highly grounded as an earth and fixed sign. It can be stubborn and stuck, but also sensual.

Gemini is the third sign, and has moved from action and being in the body to focusing on the mind. Gemini wants to come up with ideas and plans. Gemini sees the value in social connection and engagement. It can be scattered and anxious, but also adaptable.

Cancer is the fourth sign, and has moved from the mind to emotions. Cancer wants to give and receive emotional stability and security, nurturing and encouragement. It can be subjective and sensitive, but also understanding.

Leo is the fifth sign, and is okay with emotion, but wants to focus on the positives with it. Leo is highly creative, and can express itself through creativity and be seen and heard. Leo wants love and affection. It can be selfish and dramatic, but also sweet.

Virgo is the sixth sign, and moves from play to work. Virgo wants to get things done and tackle the details. Virgo sees daily life, and understands what must be done. It can be anxious and timid, but also productive.

Libra is the seventh sign, and moves from work to relationships. Libra wants to come together, to compromise and mediate. Libra wants balance and equality and fairness. It can be superficial and flighty, but also just.

Scorpio is the eighth sign, and wants to deepen those relationships. Scorpio wants everything to be intense and passionate, and won't settle. Scorpio craves intimacy and wants to transform for the better. It can be obsessive and demanding, but also loyal.

Sagittarius is the ninth sign, and it wants to let loose. Sagittarius wants space to roam, to explore, to experience life on its own terms. Sagittarius is an eternal student of life. It can be a runner and all talk, but also a great teacher.

Capricorn is the tenth sign, and it wants to clamp down and make progress. Capricorn has goals it wants to achieve and milestones it wants to hit. It has a plan, it has a focus, and it has direction. It can be distant and overly-ambitious, but also responsible.

Aquarius is the eleventh sign, and it wants to go from the traditional to the unconventional. It wants to break the status quo and push toward the future. Aquarius doesn't want to be boxed in. Aquarius has big dreams. It can be aloof and out of touch, but also independent.

Pisces is the twelfth and last sign, so it wants to ascend into the spiritual. Pisces understands all emotion and experience intuitively, and can be ultra compassionate. Pisces is imaginative. It can be sacrificing and self-sabotaging, but also inspired.
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.how-the-zodia.subject: Intro to Zodiac Signs
explain.intro.zodiac-signs.how-the-zodia.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Zodiac Signs

explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.title: Ruling planets and the natal chart
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.text: Ruling planets are important in the natal chart because they connect houses to each other. Every house in your natal chart falls in a Zodiac sign (the sign the cusp of the house falls in; the cusp of a house is the very beginning of that house). The natural planetary ruler of the sign a house falls in is the ruling planet for that house. The ruling planet for the natal house has influence over the house, so it's not just the sign the house falls in or any natal planets residing there. It's the planetary ruler too!
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.subject: Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.lineage: house rulership · ruler of the sign on the cusp
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.title: The rulers of the houses have influence over
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.text:
1st house ruler = your personality, outlook, approach
2nd house ruler = your finances, resources, values, stability, security
3rd house ruler = learning, communication
4th house ruler = home, family, foundation
5th house ruler = creativity, hobbies, romance, love, kids
6th house ruler = work, work environment, daily life, health, pets
7th house ruler = relationships, commitment, other people
8th house ruler = transformations, depths, other people's money
9th house ruler = beliefs, higher learning, travel
10th house ruler = career, goals, life path
11th house ruler = friends, dreams, future
12th house ruler = endings, what's hidden, the past, spirituality

Depending on which house system you use, you might also have a co-ruler for some of your houses. This happens when the sign the planet rules isn't on any house cusp, and is therefore intercepted (contained) in the house with the sign that comes beforehand. The signs go in order:

Aries
Taurus
Gemini
Cancer
Leo
Virgo
Libra
Scorpio
Sagittarius
Capricorn
Aquarius
Pisces

So, if you had a 10th house cusp in Scorpio and the 11th house cusp is in Capricorn, this skips over Sagittarius, and Sagittarius is intercepted in the Scorpio 10th house. This means Pluto, the ruler of Scorpio, would be the main ruler for the 10th house, and Jupiter, the ruler of Sagittarius, would be the co-ruler of the 10th house. One note: If the natural planetary ruler is in the same house that it rules in your chart, this strengthens the energy of that house and whatever it rules for you. It's a bit easier for you to use the energy. For example, if you have your 3rd house in Cancer, and your natal Moon is in the 3rd house, that makes the Cancer/Moon impact on your 3rd house extra strong.
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.subject: Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.source: Beginner Astrology - Intro to Ruling Planets in Astrology

explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.title: Ruling planets and transits
explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.text: In predictive astrology, your ruling planets are also important because whenever a transit (moving) planet is making an aspect to one of your natal planets, it's also impacting the house that planet rules in your natal chart. This means that transit planets impact your houses not only by touring them, but also by aspecting their rulers. So, when you're tracking aspects the transit planets make to your natal planets, you can consider what the planet itself rules on its own, as well as the areas of life ruled by the house the planet is the ruler of in your natal chart. For example, say your natal Mars rules your natal 7th house and is being aspected by transit Saturn. This would mean Saturn is having an impact on your energy, drive, and ability to take initiative with Mars, as well as with your relationships and dealings with others with the 7th house.

explain.intro.ruling-planets-in-astrolog.lineage: transits to house rulers · modern predictive practice
